findings.title: All-clients view permission bypasses client-specific denials
findings.body: canView() now includes fine-grained VIEW permission on the all-clients resource, so this shortcut authorizes the client before evaluating its individual resource. An administrator allowed to view all clients but explicitly denied VIEW on one client can still read that client's details and other view-protected endpoints. This contradicts hasPermission(client, ...), which applies the all-clients default only when no individual resource exists. Preserve the broad admin-role bypass, but evaluate client-specific permissions before accepting the type-level grant, and add an allow-all/deny-one test.

findings.title: Permission enumeration returns the all-clients resource name instead of client IDs
findings.body: The schema gives the all-clients resource the type Clients, so findByType includes it in this loop. When its permission is granted, the result contains the literal string "Clients", not the IDs of clients authorized by that default permission. Clients without individual authorization resources are never enumerated at all, even though hasPermission(client, scope) grants access to them. Callers filtering clients by this set therefore omit clients authorized through a type-level grant. Handle the all-clients default explicitly and enumerate actual client IDs while respecting individual overrides.

findings.title: Provision the new schema entries for existing FGAP V2 realms
findings.body: Adding Clients to SCHEMA provisions its resource and scopes only for newly initialized realms. init() immediately returns when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialized by the previous version retain only the Users resource and old scopes. Creating permissions with configure or either new mapping scope then fails in getScope(), and client evaluation can receive a null all-clients resource from its fallback lookup. Add a migration or schema synchronization path for existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: Resolve display names for the new client permission resources
findings.body: The new Clients branch creates resources whose names are internal client IDs and leaves displayName unset. However, getResourceName() still resolves only Users resources and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). It therefore returns null for individual client resources and for the schema-created all-clients resource, leaving returned permission resource-name metadata without identifiable targets. Extend getResourceName() to resolve individual clients to their clientId and give the type-level resource an All clients label.
